description: Next.js's Pages Router: the convention where the file names a PATH and no verb at all, and one default export answers every method. A frontend that knew the App Router, Remix, Nuxt and Medusa enumerated ZERO entry points of a 56,824-line application built on this one -- 54 handlers, none of them found, and a surface with nothing on it reads exactly like a surface with nothing to say. No taint findings: the expectation this corpus carries is the SURFACE, asserted route by route in surface_test.go, and the handlers here reach no dangerous sink on purpose so that anything reported would be a false positive. What it proves is that a path comes off the directory below `pages/api` wherever a monorepo puts that directory (`apps/web/` here), that `index` is the directory itself, that `[id]` is a parameter in a FILE name rather than a folder, that a catch-all is a wildcard, and that a handler branching on `req.method` -- by if-chain, by switch, or by the `!== "POST"` guard that refuses everything else -- is as many entry points as it has branches, because each branch is separately reachable and one route covering all of them would say a caller reaches the POST body through the code that answers GET. A handler that does not branch is ANY, which is what it actually serves. The negatives are the shapes that look like routes and are not. `pages/dashboard.tsx` and `pages/settings/[team].tsx` are the important ones: `pages/` without `api/` is the other half of this same convention and holds React components, identical in shape -- directory-derived path, default-exported function -- and the 38 of them in that real application would have outnumbered the 54 real routes. `schema.ts` sits under `pages/api` and exports only named helpers; Next.js serves the default export, so no URL reaches it. And a test module is a negative for the reason a test client is: it default-exports a function under `pages/api` and nothing about its shape says otherwise, but a route that exists only in a test does not exist in the program that gets deployed.
